Public Portion 
 1. Review and Discussion of the Cannabis Stabilization Fund Community Reinvestment 
Proposal. 
On October 27, 2026, the Finance Committee, chaired by Councilor Zaida Govan, met to discuss 
the proposed Cannabis Stabilization Fund Community Investment Plan and establish a process 
for distributing funds to eligible neighborhoods. Councilor Govan reviewed the existing 
ordinance, which directs cannabis tax revenue toward neighborhoods within 1.5 miles of licensed 
dispensaries for educational and recreational programming, neighborhood business incentives, 
infrastructure improvements, and community facilities. Although the ordinance originally 
contemplated allocating 50% of the City's 3% retail cannabis tax to the fund, a subsequent 
agreement set the allocation at 33%. The fund currently holds approximately $1.7 million in 
accumulated revenue. 
 
Councilor Govan presented a preliminary proposal to expend 80% of available funds annually 
while retaining 20% for future use. Suggested allocations included 30% for youth development, 
education, and prevention; 20% for behavioral health, recovery, and public health; 15% for 
workforce development and economic mobility; 10% for neighborhood revitalization and 
community safety; and 5% for community-based nonprofits. These allocations were presented as 
recommendations for further consideration rather than approved expenditures. Discussion 
included the possibility of providing property tax relief, with concerns raised regarding the 
limited financial impact and the fund's intended purpose. Members supported exploring a 
community application process modeled after the Community Preservation Act program to 
ensure accessible and equitable distribution of funds. 
 
The committee discussed establishing a working group of approximately five to seven 
representatives, potentially including City Council members, administration and finance 
representatives, public health professionals, community organizations, and residents. Councilors 
Lavar Click-Bruce and Victor Davila expressed interest in participating. Councilor Govan 
indicated that the working group could begin meeting within two weeks to develop eligibility 
guidelines, funding priorities, and an application process, with the goal of making funds 
accessible to eligible neighborhoods by January 2027. No formal vote was taken, and the 
proposed funding allocations and distribution framework remain under committee review. The 
meeting concluded at 5:18 p.m.
